page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating on the 64-bit ARM architecture, this instance features 64 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with one thread per core. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or hardware GPU accelerators, and it operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 133 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier memory performance, with uncached read memory bandwidth reaching 479.37 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth at 236.27 GB/sec. Multi-core capabilities are strong, as demonstrated by a multi-core Geekbench score of 25669.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 671.45 GB/sec. Database and key-value store operations perform in the top tier, with Redis SET operations reaching 132.72 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring 47948.79. However, single-core performance is moderate, with a single-core Geekbench score of 1888.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1706.29.

The lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware limits this instance to network-attached storage and non-GPU workloads. While LLM inference for text generation on a small 135M model is poor at 42.36 tokens/sec, text generation for medium and large models ranks as strong, processing 36.19 and 5.92 tokens/sec respectively. Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and high memory bandwidth, this instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing.
